title: Denial of Service via Panic on Untrusted Input
platform_conditions: Any Rust toolchain; panic behavior depends on release profile (panic=unwind unwinds to the nearest catch/recover, panic=abort kills the process immediately)
security_mechanism: Rust turns several ordinary mistakes into process-level aborts rather than error values: slice indexing out of range, unwrap/expect on None or Err, integer division by zero, RefCell::borrow_mut while already borrowed, and `array[index]` on fixed arrays all panic. On a shared service a panic triggered by one request aborts (panic=abort) or unwinds past the handler (unwind with no catch_unwind in the worker loop), taking the worker or whole process down. Deep recursion on attacker-shaped input (nested parsers) exhausts the fixed thread stack and raises a stack-overflow abort that no catch_unwind can catch, because it is not a Rust panic at all.

source_sink_clues.source: Request fields that select indexes, drive recursion depth, or arrive in shapes the code assumed impossible: list indexes, numeric fields used as divisors, deeply nested JSON/XML, empty optional payloads.
source_sink_clues.sink: unwrap()/expect() on input-derived Result/Option; slice/array indexing and str range slicing with external indexes; RefCell double borrow; unbounded recursion on external data

tracking_guards: Check that indexing uses .get()/.get_mut() with explicit error handling and division checks for zero, that unwrap/expect is confined to values proven by an earlier check or by construction, that recursion is bounded by an explicit depth limit, and that the worker loop installs catch_unwind (and/or the profile sets panic=unwind deliberately) so one request's panic is contained.
not_candidate_when: The index/length was validated against .len() before the access, the unwrap is backed by a preceding check that makes panic unreachable for any input, recursion depth is capped below the stack budget, or the process handles panics per-worker and the input cannot exhaust the stack.
public_references: CWE-755: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/755.html
Rust std: panic macro and catch_unwind — https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/panic/fn.catch_unwind.html
